scope: candidate mathematical/source fidelity only; not fixed-task admission or a model score

slots.objects: A uses two actual probability laws, their realizing tables, one canonical stopping time, an extended nonnegative work observable, and one real likelihood-limit witness. B constructs actual probability laws by pushing forward explicit two-bit PMFs through deterministic padding; its work is a terminal charge, not the count of active calls. These agree with the frozen reconstruction. The packet hash, candidate HEAD, and all six LF-normalized hashes matched.
slots.domains: Both results use the full product measurable space ℕ → Bool. Histories are Fin n → Bool, and the filtration sees exactly coordinates 0 through n−1 and generates the full product sigma algebra. The stopping time takes values in WithTop ℕ and work takes values in ENNReal. B is not restricted to a finite surrogate space.
slots.quantifiers: In A, the budget is imposed P-almost surely for each finite horizon; countability makes this equivalent to simultaneous P-almost-sure control at all horizons. A single L satisfies all conclusions. In B, every real m ≥ 2 has witnesses satisfying the budget at every horizon and the tail condition separately under both laws. Restriction to integer m gives the original family, and its implemented mean is unbounded.
slots.assumptions: The realization equations refer to actual cylinder masses, and both tables are normalized at every history. One-sided local support is imposed only on P-positive histories; induction gives finite-prefix Q ≪ P. A does not assume full-path absolute continuity, Q-termination, Q-integrability, bounded work, or stopped measurability of W. Omitting common deterministic padding from A weakens its hypotheses without changing the positive conclusion; B proves padding. The empty horizon under the probability law forces B ≥ 0, so no explicit premise is missing.
slots.conclusion: A proves almost-sure convergence of the actual prefix likelihoods to a strongly measurable L in L²(P), with the stated square bound, unit mean and equality of full-path measures via withDensity. It transfers finite stopping and proves finite work means under both laws and the centered variance estimate. B proves actual table realization, support, normalization, stopping at two, deterministic padding, the ideal-average bound, measurable work, ideal second moment one and implemented first moment m.
slots.senses: Real division by zero contributes zero exactly where the exercise omits zero-probability transitions; null history atoms receive zero discrepancy. A derives the first likelihood martingale identity from agreement of prefix integrals, derives the conditional square identity by summing over child atoms, and uses a predictable product compensator. Uniform integrability and measure uniqueness on the generating filtration give the full-path density. Work finiteness holds P-almost surely by the square assumption and transfers to Q before converting extended means; B integrates finite-prefix discrepancy under P, not under Q or against the likelihood.
slots.constants: A has L₀ = 1, normalized mean 1, exponent 2, square bound exp B and variance factor exp B−1. B uses p = m⁻², q = m⁻¹ and second-bit probabilities p and 1 on the first-true branch, zero on the first-false branch. Its first discrepancy is (m−1)/(m+1), the averaged second is 1−m⁻², and all later terms vanish. The all-true atom masses are m⁻⁴ and m⁻¹; charging m² gives ideal second moment 1 and implemented mean m.

uncovered_explanation: Original rubric items 1–3 are covered mathematically. Item 4 is not a Lean proposition in either signature: applying A to an actual sampler still requires a common stopped-history model, conditional likelihood and absolute continuity control, a pathwise second-moment budget, and an ideal second moment of actual total work. The cited common-suffix TV and single-phase expected-query results do not supply those interfaces. Neither actual sampler is covered.

A gives an equivalent convergence and cylinder-extension proof; it does not separately state convergence in the L² norm. B does not expose the illustrative lower bound on E_P L₂² as a conclusion. Neither is needed for the asked outcomes or the first three rubric items.
